title: Tree Models & Ensembles: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on decision trees, Gini/entropy splits, pruning, bagging and random forests, boosting (AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost) and feature importance. Ordered from mental model to a final cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Decision Trees: The Mental Model
points: A decision tree recursively splits data on one feature threshold at a time; each leaf predicts the majority class (classification) or the mean target (regression)
Greedy top-down growth: each split picks the best local gain with no look-ahead, so the tree is not globally optimal
Split on a numeric feature is a threshold test (x <= t); on a categorical feature it is a subset or one-vs-rest test
Unconstrained trees keep splitting until leaves are pure, giving zero training error and high variance (overfitting)
Trees need no feature scaling and handle non-linear interactions, but their decision boundaries are axis-aligned and unstable to small data changes

chapters.title: Gini vs Entropy Splits
points: Gini impurity = 1 - sum(p_i^2); 0 for a pure node, max 0.5 for a balanced binary node
Entropy = -sum(p_i * log2 p_i); 0 for a pure node, max 1 bit for a balanced binary node
Information gain = parent impurity minus the weighted average impurity of the children; the split with the highest gain wins
Worked example: node with 5 positives and 5 negatives has Gini 0.5 and entropy 1.0; a split into (4,1) and (1,4) gives child Gini 0.32 and a gain of 0.18
Gini vs entropy: Gini is cheaper (no log) and usually gives near-identical trees; entropy penalizes mixed nodes slightly more; regression trees use variance (MSE) reduction instead
Mistake: raw information gain favors high-cardinality features such as IDs; use gain ratio or drop ID-like columns

chapters.title: Pruning and Controlling Tree Depth
points: Pre-pruning stops growth early using max_depth, min_samples_split, min_samples_leaf or min_impurity_decrease
Post-pruning grows a full tree, then cuts back weak subtrees; sklearn implements cost-complexity pruning via ccp_alpha
Cost-complexity: minimize error + alpha * (number of leaves); larger alpha gives a smaller tree, and alpha=0 keeps the full tree
Pre vs post pruning: pre-pruning is faster but can stop too early; post-pruning is costlier but sees the full tree before cutting
Pick alpha with DecisionTreeClassifier.cost_complexity_pruning_path then cross-validate; mistake: tuning depth on the test set instead of CV

chapters.title: Bagging and Random Forests
points: Bagging = train many models on bootstrap samples (sampling with replacement) and average or vote; this reduces variance without raising bias
Each bootstrap leaves out about 36.8% of rows (1/e); these out-of-bag (OOB) rows give a free validation score via oob_score=True
Random forest = bagging of deep trees plus a random feature subset at each split (max_features: sqrt(p) for classification, about p/3 for regression), which decorrelates the trees
Bagging vs random forest: plain bagging trees stay correlated when a few strong features dominate; feature subsampling lowers the correlation and the ensemble variance
Tuning order: n_estimators (more is never overfitting, only slower), max_features, then min_samples_leaf; mistake: shallow trees, since forests want low-bias deep trees

chapters.title: Boosting: AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost
points: Boosting trains weak learners sequentially, each correcting the previous errors; it mainly reduces bias, unlike bagging which reduces variance
AdaBoost: reweights misclassified samples upward and gives each stump a vote weight alpha = 0.5 * ln((1 - err) / err)
Gradient boosting: each new tree fits the negative gradient of the loss (the residuals for squared error); update F = F + learning_rate * tree
XGBoost adds a regularized objective (L1/L2 on leaf weights, gamma per split), second-order gradients, histogram split finding, and built-in missing-value handling
Key knobs: learning_rate (small, e.g. 0.05) with more n_estimators, max_depth 3-8, subsample and colsample_bytree; use early_stopping_rounds on a validation set
Mistake: high learning rate or too many rounds with no early stopping overfits, since boosting does overfit (unlike a forest)

chapters.title: Feature Importance and Tree Models Cheat Sheet
points: Impurity-based importance (feature_importances_) sums the impurity decrease per feature; it is biased toward high-cardinality and continuous features and is computed on training data
Permutation importance shuffles one feature on held-out data and measures the score drop; it is more reliable but unreliable with highly correlated features
SHAP values give per-prediction additive attributions; TreeExplainer is fast for tree ensembles
Cheat sheet: single tree = high variance, interpretable; random forest = variance down, robust defaults; boosting = bias down, best accuracy but needs tuning and early stopping
Cheat sheet formulas: Gini = 1 - sum(p^2), Entropy = -sum(p log2 p), gain = parent minus weighted children, OOB share = 36.8%
